subject: Skyward - MAP & perf validation plan (quant + TTFT + concurrency)
messages:
From: Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@skyward-analytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reid <tom.reid@skyward-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + perf goals for model serving

Hi Tessa — thanks again for the demo last week. Tom and I discussed internally and we want to formalize the performance gating for our POC so procurement can move quickly. Can you send a short mutual action plan (MAP) that includes:
- concrete perf targets (99th pct latency, TTFT for first token, throughput/concurrency envelope)
- quantization matrix you will evaluate (FP16/BF16 -> INT8/INT4) and kernel profiling plan
- regression checks / quality guardrails we can run on our sample prompts
- expected timeline to get results so we can align procurement/ops (target close by end of month)

We care especially about TTFT at low concurrency (1–8) because our product needs snappy first-response for customer-facing features. Also include an ask list for test data, API keys, and whether we can run a quick canary in our AWS account.

Thanks,
Sylvia
Director, Platform Ops
Skyward Analytics

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@skyward-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tom Reid <tom.reid@skyward-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Skyward - MAP & perf validation plan (quant + TTFT + concurrency)

Sylvia — appreciate the clear asks. Draft MAP and benchmarking plan attached (Skyward_MAP_v1.xlsx) and summarized below. We propose a focused scope for the POC perf validation so we can hit your end-of-month close target while keeping the tests meaningful.

Summary (high level):
- Goals: 99th pct latency <= 220ms at concurrency 16 (on dedicated q4 instance), TTFT (first token) <= 55ms at concurrency 1–4, sustained throughput >= 450 tokens/s at concurrency 32 for batched workloads.
- Quantization matrix: evaluate FP16 (baseline), BF16, INT8 (per-channel symmetric), and INT4 (4-bit asymmetric) using our quant pipeline.
- Kernel profiling: run per-layer kernel latency and memory hotspot profiling across sequences [128, 512, 1024], capture kernel choices (cuBLAS/cuDNN/custom fused kernels) and kernel runtimes.
- Regression checks: run your representative prompt set (we'll take 200 prompts you provide) and compute ROUGE/EM proxies + embedding similarity; reject quantized variant if average similarity drops > 3% or top-1 correctness drop > 2%.
- Deliverables: perf matrix CSV, TTFT/concurrency plots, kernel profile CSV, MAP milestones.
- Timeline (compressed to meet end-of-month):
  * Day 0 (Dec 8): test dataset + access (you)
  * Day 1–3 (Dec 9–11): baseline runs (FP16/BF16) + kernel baseline
  * Day 4–6 (Dec 12–14): INT8 experiments + regression checks
  * Day 7–9 (Dec 15–17): INT4 experiments + final regression + stability runs
  * Day 10 (Dec 18): build final summary & docs, canary plan for your AWS account (if requested)
  * Buffer / procurement coordination: Dec 19–24; target contractual close by Dec 31.

Ask list:
- 200 labeled prompts (CSV) + 10 critical real-world dialogs for TTFT microbenchmarks
- short-lived API key for Redwood hosted test environment (we'll delete after POC)
- optional: AWS IAM role for canary (if you want runs inside your VPC)

Attachments: Skyward_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP milestones + test matrix) and a one-pager on our quantization control knobs. I'll coordinate with Karthik (kernel/profile owner) and Soojin (bench execution) once you confirm.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
Attaches: Skyward_MAP_v1.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@skyward-analytics.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tom Reid <tom.reid@skyward-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 14:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Skyward - MAP & perf validation plan (quant + TTFT + concurrency) — interim results

Sylvia / Tom / Tessa — quick status and a couple of early results from our bench (attached CSV: quant_kernel_results_20261209.csv, plots attached). Key highlights:

Baseline (FP16/BF16):
- 99th pct latency (seq512, concurrency 16): FP16=210ms, BF16=205ms
- TTFT (concurrency 1, seq128): FP16=48ms, BF16=46ms
- Throughput steady-state (seq512, concurrency 32): FP16=470 tokens/s

INT8 (post-calibration):
- 99th pct: 240ms (noticeable tail increase at high concurrency, likely kernel scheduling contention)
- TTFT: 62ms at concurrency 1 (TTFT impact driven by quant/dequant overhead for first token)
- Throughput: 620 tokens/s (substantial improvement for batched workloads)

INT4 (experimental, per-layer quant):
- 99th pct: 320ms (instability observed on seq1024 at concurrency > 8)
- TTFT: 95ms (fails our TTFT target)
- Quality: avg embedding cosine drop 2.8%, top-1 correctness drop 3.6% (triggered regression threshold)

Kernel notes (raw):
- INT8 path selects fused-int8 GEMM kernels on GPU X; observed per-layer kernel latency spikes around attention-matmul for seq>512.
- INT4 currently relies on software emulation of 4-bit ops on our platform — higher CPU overhead and non-optimal kernels.

Action items we recommend:
1) For POC, focus on INT8 for batch-heavy endpoints where throughput matters; keep FP16/BF16 for latency-sensitive interactive endpoints.
2) We will iterate on kernel scheduling and micro-batching to reduce the INT8 tail and improve TTFT; target reduction of INT8 TTFT to <=75ms by Dec 14.
3) Flag INT4 as experimental; do additional quality work if Skyward wants to pursue cost-optimal path.

Next: Soojin will run regression checks against the 200 prompts once we receive them; Vivek and I will prepare concise plots and a 1-page MAP update for procurement.

Attachments: quant_kernel_results_20261209.csv; ttft_concurrency_plots_20261209.png

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Sylvia Cho <sylvia.cho@skyward-analytics.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Procurement Ops <procurement@skyward-analytics.com>, Tom Reid <tom.reid@skyward-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Skyward - MAP & perf validation plan (quant + TTFT + concurrency) — ack and procurement next steps

Team — thanks for the rapid turnaround and the early results. We reviewed the CSV/plots and like the pragmatic recommendation to pursue INT8 for batch endpoints and FP16/BF16 for interactive flows. A few notes from procurement/ops:
- Procurement is happy to proceed with the POC ASAP; they need the MAP with milestones in the shared Drive (we saw Skyward_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short SOW that states the deliverables and acceptance criteria. Can you drop a 1-page SOW in the Drive by Monday?
- Our engineering team will upload the 200 prompts to the Drive by EOD Monday; please confirm the API key scope and rotation policy.
- For the canary run inside our VPC, we prefer a short IAM role with restricted EC2 permissions — I will loop in our cloud security lead separately.

If you can deliver the SOW + updated MAP + a one-page extract of the quant results for procurement, we will fast-track approvals. Appreciate the team moving quickly on this.

Sylvia
Director, Platform Ops | Skyward Analytics
Attachments referenced: none
